issues.failure_explanation: Substituting x_i = u_i v_i and eta_i = u_i^2/2 into the Gibbs measure gives density proportional to prod_i u_i exp(-sum_i (v_i^2 + (beta^2 lambda^2/4) u_i^2) - beta G(u odot v)) (Jacobian prod_i u_i^2, prefactor prod_i eta_i^{-1/2}): the exponent of v_i^2 has coefficient 1 and that of u_i^2 has coefficient beta^2 lambda^2/4, whereas the displayed pi has coefficient beta lambda/2 for both. The two agree only when beta lambda = 2. The displayed pi is nonetheless a valid density with the correct marginal rho (integrating out u_i v_i = x_i gives int_0^infty exp(-(beta lambda/2)(u^2 + x^2/u^2)) du = (1/2) sqrt(2 pi/(beta lambda)) exp(-beta lambda |x|)), so the defect is confined to the stated change of variables; the substitution that does produce the displayed pi is eta = u odot u/(beta lambda).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the substitution eta = u \odot u/2 by eta = u \odot u/(\beta\lambda) (equivalently rescale u), after which the displayed pi follows from eq:gibbs; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Only the derivation sentence in sec:hadamard is false; thm:overparam is independently correct and all downstream analysis uses the displayed pi, so no formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: Stated change of variables does not produce the displayed Hadamard density pi
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the substitution repairs the derivation; the displayed density, the marginal claim, and every downstream result are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof controls the singular-drift term by Holder's inequality and cor, and its own final sentence concludes (E ||u_t-u_s||^q)^{1/q} <= c |t-s|^{1/2-epsilon}, i.e. E ||.||^q <= c^q |t-s|^{q(1/2-epsilon)}, which is weaker than the stated O(|t-s|^{q/2}). The stated bound is in fact false for the u-component: for the stationary process (G=0, rho_0 = pi, an allowed initial condition) with stationary density beta lambda u exp(-beta lambda u^2/2), on the event that u stays in [a,2a] over [s,s+h] (probability of order a^2 exp(-c a^2) for h << a^2) one has int_s^{s+h} u^{-1} >= h/(2a); integrating against the stationary density over a >= h^{1/2} gives E(int_s^{s+h} u^{-1})^q of order h^{(q+3)/2} for q > 3, which is larger than O(h^{q/2}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement of part 1 to E ||(u,v)_t-(u,v)_s||^q <= c |t-s|^{q(1/2-epsilon)}, exactly matching the proved bound; no downstream change is required.
issues.overall_effect: Part 1 of timeregbnd is false as stated. Part 2 of the same proposition and the strong-error analysis (prop:error_under_bounded_ball, prop:error_discrete) only use 1/2-epsilon Holder bounds, so their stated conclusions are unaffected.
issues.title: timeregbnd part 1 states an O(|t-s|^{q/2}) bound that the proof does not give and that is false for the u-component
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local weakening of one intermediate statement; all downstream results are already stated with, and only need, 1/2-epsilon exponents, so no rate, guarantee, or scope is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The step (sum_j a_j)^{p/4} <= M^{p/4-1} sum_j a_j^{p/4} is Jensen's inequality and is valid only for p/4 >= 1, i.e. p >= 4; for 2 < p < 4 the map x^{p/4} is concave and the inequality reverses, so the displayed bound is invalid for p in (2,4). Consequently the assertion that ass:2 holds for any p>2 is unproved as written on (2,4): with the valid concave-regime estimate the resulting term Delta t^{p/4-1} T sum_j E Z_j^{p/2} produces a direct multiple of E sup Z^p whose coefficient blows up as Delta t -> 0, and the discrete Gronwall argument does not close there.

failure_location.quote: \cref{ass:2} holds for any $p>2$, and \cref{ass:ball_R} holds for any $R>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the statement to p >= 4 (sufficient for every downstream use), or replace the order-p/2 Burkholder--Davis--Gundy estimate by an order-p one: E|sum_j ((u,v)^j)^T Delta W_j|^{p/2} lesssim (E(sum_j ||Z_j||^2 Delta t)^{p/2})^{1/2} <= Delta t^{p/4} M^{p/4-1/2} (sum_j E Z_j^p)^{1/2} <= T^{p/4} (E sup Z^p)^{1/2}, which closes via Young's inequality.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the pth-moment bound for the numerical scheme is established only for p >= 4. Since prop:error_discrete and thm:num_conv require only some p>2, all downstream conclusions survive by taking p >= 4.
issues.title: Moment-bound proof applies Jensen in the wrong direction for 2<p<4, leaving 'ass:2 holds for any p>2' unproved in that range
issues.why_classification: The fix is contained (take p >= 4, or one order-p BDG estimate) and loses nothing: the downstream theory needs only some p>2, and the moment bound itself is true.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: An easy corollary of \cref{lem:2ndmoments_discrete} is that  $\pi_\tstep(V)$ (for $V((u,v))=1+\norm{(u,v)}^2$) is bounded uniformly in $\tstep$.

issues.failure_explanation: The key step E_{1,T}(Delta t) -> 0 is the finite-time discretization error with both processes started from the truncated invariant measure tilde pi_{Delta t}, and the proof invokes thm:num_conv for it. But thm:num_conv requires reg3(ii), i.e. rho_0/pi uniformly bounded, which is never verified for tilde pi_{Delta t}: truncation on B_R yields uniform moments (pi_{Delta t}(V) bounded) but does not bound the density ratio tilde pi_{Delta t}/pi (that would require pi_{Delta t} to vanish on {u_i = 0} at least like u_i, which is unestablished). The hypothesis is essential: the finite-time error analysis relies on cor and timeregbnd, whose inverse-moment bounds come from prop:l1 under h_0 in L^infinity(pi); from the established facts one only gets tilde pi_{Delta t}/pi in L^p(pi) for p < 2 (since pi behaves like prod u_i at the boundary), which via prop:l1 yields E u_{i,t}^{-r} < infinity only for r < 1, insufficient for the epsilon in (0,1/2) time-regularity bounds needed already on the first step [0, Delta t]. (The proof's final display also writes |pi_{Delta t}(phi) - pi(phi)| = epsilon instead of <= epsilon.)

failure_location.quote: If $\pi_\tstep$ does not satisfy \cref{reg3}, we may replace $\pi_\tstep$ with  a regularised distribution $\tilde \pi_\tstep$. ... Then, for any $T>0$, $E_{1,T}(\tstep)\\to 0$ as $\tstep\to 0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compare both processes started from rho_0 = pi (which satisfies reg3(ii) with rho_0/pi = 1): |pi_{Delta t}(phi) - pi(phi)| <= |pi_{Delta t}(phi) - pi P^k phi| + |pi P^k phi - P_T phi| + |P_T phi - pi(phi)|, bounded respectively by C e^{-rho k} via num_erg, by thm:num_conv, and by C e^{-rho T} pi(V) via erg2; then take T large and Delta t -> 0. This uses only results already proved in the paper and loses nothing.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of convergence of the stationary distribution pi_{Delta t} to pi for Lipschitz test functions has a genuine gap at the truncation step; the theorem's conclusion remains valid but is not established as written.
issues.title: Convergence to the invariant measure: the finite-time convergence theorem is applied with an initial distribution not shown to satisfy its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: Repairing the gap requires reworking the proof of the final convergence theorem (replacing the truncation argument by the three-term comparison above), a contained but nontrivial change; however it needs no new proof architecture and the conclusion, guarantee type, and scope all survive, so it is moderate rather than serious.
